To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recurrent networks of neurons with noisy spiking behavior can perform approximate Bayesian inferences in dynamic and hierarchical graphical networks.

(1) the membrane potential dynamics of noisy integrate-and fire neurons can implement belief propagation in graphical models and (2) the spiking probability can approximate the posterior probability in the log domain, given past inputs.

(1) recurrent networks of noisy neurons can implement Bayesian inference for dynamic graphical models, (2) the posterior probability of a neuron's preferred state is approximately represented by the neuron's spiking probability, and (3) a two-level network with a hierarchy of neurons that implement approximate Bayesian inference can produce attentional effects in V2 and beyond.
